result: Core phone deployment and functional verification passed with sandbox limitations

installation.method: Official npm package in a private mount namespace and chroot; upstream package not patched
installation.modelExecution: DeepSeek API; Harness and command tools execute on the phone

resolvedIssues: Initial Android toybox mount incompatibility caused blocked mount tasks. Approved reboot cleared them. Launcher now uses Ubuntu util-linux mount, verifies private propagation, and leaves zero verification mounts in the host namespace.

On this phone, Chrome external-intent navigation repeatedly landed on HTTP 401. Direct address-bar navigation succeeded. The open helper now performs this navigation after the launch-token exchange without changing server authentication.
limitations: The phone kernel does not provide usable Landlock; default workspace-write command sandbox fails closed. Tested commands ran with the Harness full-access mode under UID 2000 and dropped Linux capabilities. This is not a complete security sandbox.
Boot autostart is not configured; start the service manually after reboot.
USB unplugged operation and long-duration standby were not tested.
The open helper requires the phone to be unlocked and uses the installed Chrome browser.
